independent_input_declaration.declaration: Independently graded both full original entries for each Q01–Q18 using only the two allowed inputs, fully read before grading. No other files, web sources, prior results, other blocks, agents, or thread/status tools were consulted. Every same-entry substantive field was assessed; restated questions and labels were treated as scaffolding. No facts were borrowed across questions.

text_read_receipts.reading_method: Literal contiguous Unicode-character slices, each at most 6000 characters; each tool output configured for 5000 tokens and returned without truncation.
Literal contiguous Unicode-character slices, each at most 6000 characters; each tool output configured for 5000 tokens and returned without truncation.

grading_policy: Correct requires all actually asked facts resolved with summary support and no material false assertion or unsupported guessing. Complete operative same-entry quotations may supply ordinary lookup facts; concrete calculations require an actual answer. Context is checked for falsehoods without additional omission gates. Equivalent wording and concrete applications are accepted.

technical_issues.issue: The initial metadata command used unavailable python; it produced no input text.
technical_issues.resolution: Retried successfully with python3, then fully read both inputs in contiguous slices.

required_facts.reason: Answer gives Trade → Economy → Confluence, matching the summary ordinary turn order.
Answer expressly ends Trade when all but one player are done.
Answer expressly permits immediate invention before running Economy.

results.whole_entry_assessment: All three asked clauses are directly answered. The entire entry, including phase details and quoted Trade rules, agrees with the summary.

required_facts.reason: Answer actually computes the requested penalty: 2 for the card + 2 for the octagon + 2 for the two cubes + 1 for the ship = 7 points.
Answer expressly permits the resulting score to become negative.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry gives the concrete seven-point loss and negative-score conclusion, with correct performance procedure and tariff. All substantive fields are consistent with the summary.

required_facts.reason: Answer identifies the species-background economic card as a loan returning at the end of that turn.
Answer expressly makes the colony transfer permanent.
Answer expressly makes the research-team transfer permanent.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry distinguishes the temporary species-card loan from permanent colony and research-team transfers and supplies the loan-return timing. No same-entry contradiction appears.

required_facts.reason: Answer specifies running a controlled research team’s violet converter during Trade.
Answer specifies paying one complete alternative printed input set, rather than combining alternatives.
Answer expressly flips the research team upon invention.
Answer immediately puts the inventor’s matching species card into play.

Answer gives Confluence after that Economy as the ordinary sharing time; its same-entry invention quote explicitly identifies Yengii inventions as private and era-IV inventions as unique, qualifying that ordinary rule.
Answer explicitly defers collection of the Sharing Bonus until Confluence.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The answer and complete operative same-entry quotations jointly resolve invention procedure, alternative cost, flipping, immediate inventor access, qualified Confluence sharing, and bonus timing. The general sharing sentence is qualified by the entry’s explicit Yengii and era-IV exception text; it does not expressly override those exceptions.

required_facts.reason: Answer requires both target and payment card to be in play with their own owner and neither on loan.
Answer places the spent card underneath the flipped target.
Answer explicitly denies a renamed upgraded card eligibility to pay an upgrade requiring its former name.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry correctly resolves ownership, in-play status, the spent-card destination, and renamed-card ineligibility. Its additional upgrade context agrees with the summary.

required_facts.reason: Answer places the Colony Support check at the beginning of Economy before production.
Answer puts excess colonies beneath the colony deck.
Answer explicitly makes white economic converters optional.
Answer gives the normal maximum of one use; the same-entry Economy quote expressly preserves species exceptions.
Answer explicitly forbids using one economic converter’s output to fund another in the same Economy.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry correctly resolves the support check, excess destination, optional and normally once-per-turn operation, exceptions, and simultaneous production. No substantive field permits chaining.

required_facts.reason: Answer keeps donation goods in the donation area until traded or gifted.
Answer requires disposal in the next Trade and gifting any remainder at its end.
Answer expressly says the recipient cannot refuse the gift.
Answer expressly allows donation victory points to be traded.

results.whole_entry_assessment: All donation disposition, gift-refusal, and tradable-point clauses are resolved. The quoted final-Economy exception also agrees with the summary.

required_facts.reason: Answer gives the secret colony/research/retained division; its complete same-entry bid quote additionally requires announcing total ships first and explicitly allows empty piles.
Answer expressly commits both bids before revealing either.
Answer resolves colonies before research and uses descending bid order.
Answer concretely spends all five ships on the minimum-two purchase; the same-entry bid quote limits each ordinary purchase opportunity to one eligible card.
Answer expressly retains ships on a pass and requires passing when no legal card remains.
The complete same-entry bid quote explicitly makes each reveal simultaneous and places the research reveal after all colony choices.
The complete same-entry bid quote explicitly orders equal bids by fewer cards of the relevant type, then higher printed species tiebreak.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The concrete payment and pass conclusions are correct. The complete operative bid quotation supplies announcement, empty-pile permission, simultaneous reveals, single-card eligibility, and tie order where the answer abbreviates them. All substantive fields remain consistent.

required_facts.reason: Answer removes all remaining cards currently at minimum bid 1 after bidding.
Answer puts those cards beneath their respective decks front-side up.
Answer slides survivors fully left.
Answer refills empty right spaces from the matching deck top front-side up; the same-entry bid quote expressly adds without flipping.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry correctly identifies minimum-one leftovers, respective deck-bottom destinations, face-up orientation, left shift, and right refill from the top without flipping. All facts are resolved within this entry.

required_facts.reason: Answer retains the producer’s last-Economy donation output, corroborated by the same-entry scoring quote.
Answer provides the actual total of 3 points: 1 for two octagons, 1 for four large cubes, and 1 for the combined six small cubes/ships.
Answer expressly says there is no final-score tiebreaker.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry supplies the actual three-point result, final donation retention, and absence of a tiebreaker. Six combined small cubes/ships correctly contribute one point; no additional general-formula narration is required.

required_facts.reason: Answer actually gives five committed ships an effective colony bid of 2½, correctly applying the no-rounding halving rule.
Answer adds a seedling on a Caylion colony acquisition from the bid track.
Answer expressly retains the seedling through upgrading and trading the colony.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry gives the actual 2½ bid and resolves seedling acquisition and persistence. Its same-entry context also correctly distinguishes starting colonies and colonies received through trade.

required_facts.reason: Answer expressly prohibits Eni Et running their own interest converters, including upgraded ones.
Answer expressly permits Eni Et upgrading those cards.
Answer gives the actual four-cube output: the same one large Unity wild plus three large blue cubes, matching the summary’s exact example.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry supplies the Eni Et use restriction, permission to upgrade, and the actual requested four-cube output. Its complete Eni Et quote preserves the original wild and prohibits creating more wilds. The final sentence calling both inputs “preserved” is imprecise about the physical ordinary blue cube, but does not change the explicit output, color, size, rate, or wild count; it is not a material rules contradiction.
nonmaterial_notes: The summary specifically requires physical preservation of the wild. Retaining an indistinguishable ordinary blue input as part of the three-blue output does not change the substantive result.

required_facts.reason: Answer expressly prohibits a non-Faderan holder trading Acknowledgments away.
Answer requires one token to return to Faderan on each invention while tokens are held, so the inventor cannot save the required tokens.
Answer actually applies the rule to both inventions and returns two tokens to Faderan.
Answer actually awards Faderan two points; its same-entry Acknowledgments quote explicitly sources each point from the common pool.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry correctly forbids non-Faderan token transfers, requires one return per invention, and concretely returns two tokens for two Faderan points. The same-entry operative quote identifies the common pool as the point source.

required_facts.reason: Answer requires shuffling the relic deck before play and keeping it face down.
Answer identifies all deck backs as one converter, rather than separate activations per card.
Answer places the back converter in Trade at most once per turn.
Answer gives the Detector’s additional cost as one colony of any climate and three green cubes.
Answer explicitly permits the Detector to provide a second relic draw in the same turn as the ordinary back converter.

results.whole_entry_assessment: All asked deck preparation, activation count, phase/frequency, Detector cost, and second-draw facts are resolved. The complete quotation also includes the nullspace removal exception to the ordinary consumed-colony destination.

required_facts.reason: The complete same-entry Fleet Support quote explicitly requires matching every required support symbol with available fleet support.
Answer expressly permits dividing one fleet’s support among several cards.
Answer expressly permits combining multiple fleets’ support on one card.
Answer requires sufficient fleet support to accompany a support-requiring loan so the borrower can run it.
Answer expressly exempts borrowed cards lacking support symbols from fleet-support requirements.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The answer and full same-entry Fleet Support quote resolve every required support symbol, both allocation directions, accompanying support for loans, and the no-symbol exemption. Other quoted Im’dril context is consistent.

required_facts.reason: Answer chooses the split at Kjas’s colony-bid opportunity; its same-entry Military Might quote identifies this as the normal buy/pass opportunity.
Answer actually splits five into three and two; the quote confirms this is the required even-as-possible division.
Answer expressly prohibits splitting again that turn.
Answer recalculates the current colony count between halves, including the first purchase, for the second half’s tie.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry gives the normal decision timing, actual three/two split, prohibition on further splits that turn, and updated colony count for the second tie. Extra timing and setup context is consistent.

required_facts.reason: Answer keeps the depicted starting pairs together; the same-entry Nonlinear Thinking quote explicitly forbids both splitting and rearranging.
Answer expressly permits each half to upgrade independently.
Answer expressly permits loaning the intact pair as one card.
Answer enters a nullspace colony through its top converter during Trade.
Answer expressly permits permanent transfer of nullspace colonies.
Answer expressly removes consumed nullspace colonies from the game, corroborated by the quote distinguishing removal from the colony-deck bottom.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry resolves fixed paired cards, independent upgrades, intact-pair loans, Trade entry via top converter, permanent nullspace transfer, and removal upon consumption. The complete quote supplies explicit no-rearrangement language and the ordinary-deck contrast.

required_facts.reason: Answer gives black, blue, and yellow as the large Unity wild substitutions.
Answer gives green, white, and brown as the small Unity wild substitutions.
Answer permits different colors; the complete same-entry Flexible Input quote explicitly accepts differently colored cubes of the depicted size.
Answer expressly prohibits Zeth stealing Unity wild resources.

results.whole_entry_assessment: The entry resolves both color lists, mixed-color input permission, and immunity to Zeth theft, using its own complete Unity quote where needed. Additional species context is consistent with the summary.
